info.title: SynCloud API
info.description: The public SynCloud controller API. The dashboard, synctl and CI all use these endpoints (plan §5.1). Authenticate with the dashboard session cookie, a personal access token (Bearer), or a signed access-key request (SYN1-HMAC-SHA256, plan §7.1).

post.summary: Upgrade the controller (rolls back automatically when unhealthy)
post.description: Downloads and verifies the release, snapshots the database, and hands over to a guard that restarts the controller with the new binary. If it is not healthy within the timeout, or stops being healthy while settling, the previous binary and database are restored. version defaults to the newest on the release channel.

get.summary: Agent versions per node and the last rollout

post.summary: Upgrade agents node by node to the controller's version
post.description: Each node receives the agent binary over its stream, restarts into it (containers keep running) and must reconnect with the new version before the next node starts; a node whose new agent does not reconnect restores the old one. A failure stops the rollout. nodes (IDs or names) defaults to every node; force re-sends to nodes already at the target.

post.summary: A single-use command that re-joins an existing node (ID or name)
post.description: For a reinstalled or restored host: the node keeps its ID, pool and tasks and gets a new certificate; the old one stops working.

tags.description: also build new tags matching this pattern, e.g. v* (empty: tags are ignored)

paths.description: only build commits that change a matching file ("!" excludes; * matches across directories), e.g. services/api/**

refs.description: watched branches and tags with their last seen commit

webhook.description: how pushes arrive: a webhook SynCloud created, the GitHub App's, or one to add by hand

branch.description: branch to build, or a pattern such as release/* (every matching branch is built)

tags.description: also build new tags matching this pattern, e.g. v* (empty: tags are ignored)

paths.description: only build commits that change a matching file ("!" excludes; * matches across directories), e.g. services/api/**

builder.description: auto: the Dockerfile, else Nixpacks, else a static site (index.html served by nginx on port 80)

repo.description: owner/name on that connection; the branch defaults to the repository's default branch

GitSourceInput.description: Give url (any Git host), or connection and repo (a connected provider: SynCloud then creates the webhook and reports commit statuses).

status.description: skipped: no changed file matched the path filters

runId.description: the job run that executes the build; its logs are the build log

baseSha.description: the previous commit of the ref, which path filters compare with

charts.description: cpu (percent of one core), memory (bytes), netRx, netTx, diskRead, diskWrite (bytes/s)

priority.description: lower runs first; an image belongs to the first rule whose prefix matches

keepLast.description: keep the newest N, expire the rest (set this or olderThanDays)

olderThanDays.description: expire images created more than N days ago

inUse.description: used by a service's current or previous revision; never expired

host.description: registry host, e.g. docker.io or ghcr.io

actor.description: user email, node, build or controller

RouteTraffic.description: one routed service's traffic over the summary window

charts.description: requests (series per status class 2xx…5xx, req/s), latency (p50/p95/p99, ms), bandwidth (in/out, bytes/s) and, beyond one service, services (req/s per service)

metric.description: cpu and memory: % of the reservation (average per task); rps: requests/s per task; latency: p95 in ms

scaleOutCooldown.description: seconds after a change before scaling out again

scaleInCooldown.description: seconds after a change before scaling in

scaleInChecks.description: consecutive 15s evaluations below target before scaling in

value.description: the metric at the last evaluation (null: no data)

reason.description: e.g. cpu 82 > target 60 % of reserved CPU → 3→5 tasks

AlertChannelConfig.description: write-only (sealed at rest); the fields of the channel's type

summary.description: what it sends to, without secrets

forSeconds.description: the condition must hold this long before firing

delivery.description: per channel: ok or the error

peers.description: any, cluster, IPv4/CIDR, group:[project/]name, service:[project/]env/name, environment:self|[project/]env, project:self|name

config.description: type-specific: rate-limit {average, burst}; basic-auth {users: [{username, password}], realm} (passwords are write-only); ip-allowlist {sourceRange}; security-headers {hsts, hstsSeconds, frameDeny, noSniff, referrerPolicy}; cors {origins, methods, headers, credentials, maxAge}; circuit-breaker {expression}; retry {attempts}; redirect-www and compress {}

services.description: attached services, ENV/NAME: every HTTP route of each uses it

TraefikSettings.description: Global Traefik options for every replica (§5.7). Static options restart Traefik; dynamic ones apply within seconds.

readTimeout.description: Entrypoint read timeout, e.g. 60s (empty = Traefik default)

trustedIPs.description: Proxies whose X-Forwarded-* headers are trusted (IPs or CIDRs)

installUrl.description: adds the GitHub App to more accounts or repositories
